name: firecrawl-mcp

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, or a targeted answer. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages. `url` may omit the scheme (`example.com/page`); it is read as https.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. Browser actions can change the live page when interactive actions are enabled. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Enumerate URLs indexed under one website through Firecrawl without fetching each page's content. Use this when the request asks for a site's URL inventory, when several relevant pages must be located, or when the desired page URL is unknown. An optional `search` term narrows the URL list, while sitemap, subdomain, query-parameter, and result-limit options control coverage.

`url` may omit the scheme (`example.com`); it is read as https. Returns matching URLs rather than page bodies. Retrieve one page with `firecrawl_scrape`; collect content across multiple pages with `firecrawl_crawl`. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional map feedback.

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Use this when you need current or specific information from the web: recent events, latest releases and versions, prices, people and companies, statistics, or any fact that may have changed since your training data or that you are not sure of. Returns ranked results with query-relevant highlights; each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. alexandria_library_read runs a selected capability; alexandria_library_search explores the whole library and reads full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Read a selected tool's contract with alexandria_library_search.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Browse the whole library with alexandria_library_search.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

scrapeOptions.description: Fetches the full page of every web result in the same call, and each fetched result is billed as a scrape. Leave it unset unless the task needs the full text of a few results: highlights usually answer, and firecrawl_scrape can fetch only the URLs you need. These fetches ignore maxAge, so use firecrawl_scrape for a live fetch. scrapeOptions fetches web pages, never Alexandria provider tools.

tools.name: firecrawl_find_tools
tools.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

tools.name: alexandria_library_search
tools.description: Explore the Alexandria library: Firecrawl's catalogue of data providers that return typed, sourced records (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more) as a read-only filesystem, using shell commands. Use this to find out whether a provider covers the data a task needs, and to read its contract before alexandria_library_read. Layout: /library/<category>/<provider>/<capability>.md, one file per capability holding its contract (when to use it, inputs, outputs, and the call to send); /library, each category folder and each provider folder has a README.md describing what is inside. Category folders: agriculture, ai-models, apps, automotive, community, companies, developer, digital-intelligence, education, energy, entertainment, finance, game-development, government, health, healthcare, jobs, knowledge, life-sciences, marketing, music, news, people, places, podcasts, political-science, real-estate, research, restaurants, shopping, skills, social, software, sports, travel; `ls /library` shows any added since. Available commands: ls, tree, cat, head, tail, grep, find, wc, sort, uniq, cut, tr, sed, jq, xargs, with pipes. Typical starts: `ls /library`, `cat /library/README.md`, or `grep -ril "mortgage" /library`. A file path is the execute address: /library/finance/fred/series/observations.md is provider "fred", capability "series/observations". Recorded example responses are under /examples/<provider>/<capability>.json. Free; does not run providers.

command.description: Shell command to run inside the read-only library, e.g. `grep -ril "rental" /library | head -20`.

tools.name: alexandria_library_read
tools.description: Run capabilities of Alexandria data providers and return their typed, sourced records: one, or up to ten in one call when a task needs several lookups. Alexandria is Firecrawl's library of data providers across companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more. For people and company enrichment or search, use people_company_enrich or people_company_search when they are listed; call a provider here directly only when the user asks for that provider. Each entry of `calls` is {provider, capability, options}: `provider` and `capability` come from firecrawl_search results or alexandria_library_search, and `options` follow the capability's contract, which marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group). Where the contract declares pagination, its fields page through results with the same filters. Returns one result per call, in the same order, in data.alexandria, each with data, records, or an error with a code; one call can fail while the others succeed, and an invalid call returns an error naming the valid options. A result too large to return inline is retained, and nextTool reads it in slices. Billed per executed capability; discovery is free. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

calls.description: The capabilities to run, 1-10, each {provider, capability, options}. Results come back in the same order.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

tools.name: firecrawl_search_feedback
tools.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

tools.name: firecrawl_feedback
tools.description:
Submit concise quality feedback for a completed search, scrape, parse, or map job. Provide the endpoint, job ID, rating, and relevant issue codes or small contextual fields; omit large page contents and raw outputs.

For an Alexandria session, set endpoint to `alexandria`, omit jobId, and provide requestedWebsite (url and requestedFunctionality), objective, rationale, and rating. objective is the underlying goal behind the session: what you or your user were ultimately trying to accomplish (for example, "shortlist federal IT contracts to bid on this quarter"), not only what was needed from this website. Optional providerFeedback and capabilityFeedback describe gaps or errors. Capability issues: new_capability_request (requires requestedFunctionality), missing_capability, insufficient_functionality, incorrect_result, execution_error, other. Alexandria results carry a feedbackRef per call. The overall rating covers every call in this session; callRatings [{ref, rating}] rate individual calls by feedbackRef. Alexandria feedback must arrive within 20 minutes of the team's latest Alexandria search, discovery, or execution; later feedback is rejected. Eligible feedback can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to daily caps per website and per team.

Returns submission status, feedback ID, and accounting fields.

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Start a multi-page crawl at a website URL, poll it to a terminal state, and return the final status and collected data. Scope can be bounded with include/exclude paths, depth, page limit, subdomain/external-link controls, sitemap handling, delay, and scrape options.

Crawl results can be large; use conservative limits when full-site coverage is unnecessary. Webhooks and interactive scrape actions are unavailable in safe mode. `zeroDataRetention` runs the crawl with zero data retention and requires an eligible authenticated account. Returns the crawl ID, status, and page data.

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status
tools.description: Retrieve the current status, progress, and available results for an existing crawl ID. This only reads Firecrawl job state and does not start or modify the crawl.

tools.name: firecrawl_agent
tools.description:
Run web research that returns structured data when the URLs are not known or the answer spans several sites. Describe the fields you need in `prompt`, optionally pass a JSON `schema` and seed `urls`, and the research agent searches, navigates, reads pages, and returns JSON assembled across sources. Use it to research an entity plus its fields (founders, pricing, contact details), to build lists and datasets (companies, people, products, jobs, papers), and for pages that need navigation or interaction to reach the data. Optional `effort` sets the reasoning budget, `maxCredits` caps spend, and `strictConstrainToURLs` keeps the agent to the supplied `urls`.

This call returns only a job ID, not the research result. Read the job with `firecrawl_agent_status` until it reaches `completed` or `failed`; a typical research run takes one to three minutes. For one known URL use `firecrawl_scrape` (with formats: ["markdown"], then extract the requested fields yourself); for a plain lookup that a results page answers, use `firecrawl_search`.

The job also returns a `threadId`. To continue that thread, pass it with a follow-up `prompt`; omitted `mode`, `urls`, `schema` and exchange settings carry over from the previous turn.

The agent only calls Alexandria providers whose terms the team has accepted. `exchange.skippedProviders` lists gated providers. With `exchange.onTermsRequired` "ask", a terms `pendingApproval` and `exchange.requiresAction` carry the `approvalId` and provider requirements. Read terms/show through `firecrawl_scrape`. An organization admin must accept terms in the Firecrawl dashboard at the provider URL or https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=data-sources. Ignore any terms/accept call in the API response. Only after the admin confirms acceptance, resume with the same `threadId` and `exchange.approve: {approvalId}`; this does not accept terms. To decline, use `exchange.decline: {approvalId}`. Never infer acceptance from a data request.

effort.description: Reasoning budget for the agent task.

maxCredits.description: Spending limit in credits for this run. Defaults to 2500 on the API.

strictConstrainToURLs.description: If true, agent will only visit URLs provided in the urls array.

threadId.description: Continue this thread: the threadId from an earlier firecrawl_agent or firecrawl_agent_status result. Omit to start a new thread.

mode.description: "extract" (default) returns the complete structured result every turn. "chat" lets a follow-up that asks no new data get a short reply in message instead of a re-run; required for exchange.requireApproval. Omitted on a follow-up keeps the previous turn's mode.

enabled.description: Let the agent call Alexandria providers. On by default.

toolkits.description: Pin up to 5 providers the agent may use, by slug. Omitted means the whole catalog.

maxCalls.description: Most provider calls the agent may make in this turn.

requireApproval.description: End the turn with a paid-call pendingApproval before any paid provider call. Requires mode "chat" on the same request, even on a follow-up.

approve.description: Answer yes to the pendingApproval the previous turn of this thread ended on (its id, also exchange.requiresAction.approvalId). Needs threadId. For a terms offer, send it only after an organization admin confirms acceptance in the Firecrawl dashboard; this does not accept terms. callIds and always are ignored on terms offers. For paid calls, callIds picks a subset (default all) and always stops asking for the rest of the thread.

decline.description: Answer no to that pendingApproval. Needs threadId. A declined terms offer keeps those providers out of the rest of the thread.

onTermsRequired.description: What to do when a provider the agent would use needs data terms the team has not accepted. Gated providers are never called. "skip" (default): answer with accepted providers and list the rest in exchange.skippedProviders. "ask": the same, plus a terms pendingApproval and exchange.requiresAction. Read terms with terms/show; an organization admin accepts them in the Firecrawl dashboard. There is no auto-accept. Omitted on a follow-up keeps the previous turn's value.

exchange.description: Alexandria provider settings for this turn, forwarded as the request's exchange object.

zeroDataRetention.description: Run with zero data retention. Requires an eligible authenticated account with Zero Data Retention enabled for both scrape and search. Cannot be combined with threadId.

tools.name: firecrawl_agent_status
tools.description:
Retrieve progress or final results for a `firecrawl_agent` job ID. A `processing` response is non-terminal and does not contain the final research result. Check again after 15–30 seconds until the status is `completed` or `failed`; a typical research run takes one to three minutes and complex jobs can take longer. If the job cannot finish within the task's available time, use `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_scrape` to complete the requested output.

Returns job status, progress information, and result data when completed.

tools.name: firecrawl_interact
tools.description:
Open or reuse a live browser session to navigate a page, click controls, fill and submit forms, or run browser code. Provide either `url` (the scheme may be omitted) or `scrapeId`, and either a natural-language `prompt` or executable `code`; code can run as Bash, Python, or Node with a bounded timeout.

The session runs in an isolated Firecrawl-hosted browser that never receives the end user's own browser cookies or credentials. By default it starts with no cookies or saved sessions; an optional team-scoped `scrapeOptions.profile` reuses state saved by the team's earlier sessions. Actions run on the live site, so submitting a form can have effects on that site. Returns execution output, stdout/stderr, exit status, and session viewing URLs. When the page needs the user to act, share `interactiveLiveViewUrl` with the user only, so they can take over the session.

tools.name: firecrawl_interact_stop
tools.description: Stop the live interact session associated with a `scrapeId` and release its resources. Returns a success confirmation.

tools.name: firecrawl_parse
tools.description:
Parse one supported document into markdown, HTML, links, summary, targeted answers, or JSON matching a schema. Supported inputs include common HTML, PDF, Word, RTF, OpenDocument, and spreadsheet files; PDF parsing can be bounded with `pdfOptions.maxPages`.

Local MCP reads `filePath` from the server filesystem. Hosted MCP uses two calls: first provide `filePath` to receive upload instructions, upload locally, then call again with the returned `uploadRef`; do not send both fields together. Remote web URLs belong in `firecrawl_scrape`.

Set `redactPII` to request redaction of personally identifiable information in the returned content. `zeroDataRetention` requires an eligible authenticated account; omit it for anonymous keyless use. Returns upload instructions for hosted phase one or parsed document content for the final call. Authenticated final responses can include a `data.metadata.scrapeId` for optional parse feedback.

maxAge.description: Ignored: parse never reuses or stores indexed content.

filePath.description: Absolute or relative path to a local file to parse. Supported: .html, .htm, .pdf, .docx, .doc, .odt, .rtf, .xlsx, .xls

contentType.description: Optional MIME type override. If omitted, the server infers the file kind from the extension.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_create
tools.description:
Create a recurring scrape, crawl, or search monitor that compares each check with its retained predecessor. The simple form accepts `page`/`pages` or `queries` plus a plain-language `goal`; the advanced `body` form controls targets, schedule, change-tracking formats, judging, retention, webhook, and notifications.

In the simple form, a `goal` is required. If `queries` contains one or more non-empty values and is supplied with `page`/`pages`, `queries` create the search target and page targets are ignored. A monitor schedules future network checks and can send configured email or webhook notifications. Returns the created monitor.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_list
tools.description: List monitors for the authenticated account with optional pagination controls. Returns one page of monitor records and pagination metadata.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_get
tools.description: Retrieve one monitor by ID, including its configuration and current state. This does not run or modify the monitor.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_update
tools.description:
Patch an existing monitor by ID; changes affect future scheduled checks. Pause or resume it with `status` ("paused" or "active"). Reschedule it with `scheduleText` (plain language, e.g. "every 6 hours") or `cron`, plus `timezone`; a new schedule without `timezone` runs in UTC. For other fields pass `body`, a partial monitor in the create shape (name, targets, goal, judgeEnabled, webhook, notification, retentionDays), e.g. `{"name": "Pricing watch"}`. The parameters are merged into `body` as `{"status": ..., "schedule": {"text" or "cron": ..., "timezone": ...}}` and override the same keys there. At least one change is required.

Returns the updated monitor.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete a monitor by ID and stop its future schedule. This operation cannot be undone and returns deletion status.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_run
tools.description: Queue an immediate check for a monitor outside its normal schedule. This starts network work for the monitor's configured targets and returns the queued check.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_checks
tools.description: List historical checks for a monitor, optionally filtered by status and bounded by a result limit. Returns one page of check summaries and pagination metadata.

tools.name: firecrawl_monitor_check
tools.description:
Retrieve one monitor check and its page-level results, optionally filtered by page status. Pages report `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed`, or `error`; configured goal judging can add a meaningful-change decision.

Markdown tracking returns a unified text diff, JSON tracking returns field paths with previous/current values and a current snapshot, and mixed tracking returns both. Returns one page of results plus a `next` URL when more pages exist.

tools.name: firecrawl_research_search_papers
tools.description:
Search paper metadata and abstracts with a natural-language query across the indexed corpus, which spans biomedical, life-science, and clinical literature (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) alongside arXiv and other scientific sources. Optional author, category, date, and sort options constrain or reorder results.

Several distinct framings of the same question surface different papers than a single query does.

Returns ranked papers with canonical IDs, titles, authors, and abstracts.

query.description: Natural-language research topic or question, including methods, systems, conditions, populations, interventions, or outcomes when relevant.

k.description: Number of ranked papers to return (default 40).

authors.description: Author substring filter(s); ALL must match (case-insensitive).

categories.description: Paper category filter(s) (e.g. `cs.LG`); ALL provided values must match.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound on created/updated date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

to.description: Inclusive upper bound on created/updated date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

sort.description: `relevance` (default) or `date_desc`, which returns the newest of the most relevant matches, newest first by created date. It does not list every paper in a date range; add `from` (and `to`) for that.

tools.name: firecrawl_research_inspect_paper
tools.description: Retrieve canonical metadata for one paper ID, such as an arXiv, PMC, PMID, or DOI identifier. Returns the title, abstract, authors, categories, source IDs, and dates as markdown.

paperId.description: Canonical paperId or primaryId such as `arxiv:1706.03762`, `pmcid:PMC12530322`, `pmid:40953549`, or `doi:10.1016/j.neunet.2025.108095`.

tools.name: firecrawl_research_related_papers
tools.description:
Find citation-graph candidates from one to ten `seed_ids`; the first ID is the primary seed and later IDs are anchors. `mode` defaults to `similar` (co-citation/bibliographic coupling); `citers` returns papers citing a seed and `references` papers cited by a seed. `intent` ranks candidates.

Returns ranked candidates and the evaluated pool size.

rerank.description: Apply an additional rerank over the fused candidates.

tools.name: firecrawl_research_read_paper
tools.description:
Retrieve in-body passages from one paper that are relevant to a specific question. Full text is available only for indexed papers; `k` controls the number of passages.

Returns matching passages or a notice when full text is unavailable.

paperId.description: Canonical paperId or primaryId such as `arxiv:1706.03762`, `pmcid:PMC12530322`, `pmid:40953549`, or `doi:10.1016/j.neunet.2025.108095`.

tools.name: firecrawl_developer_search
tools.description:
Search an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation for programming questions that need external documentation or upstream evidence.

Returns ranked results with an ID, source type, URL, title, and the matched passages in markdown.

query.description: Natural-language developer question or search phrase, including the library, error message, or API involved when relevant.

k.description: Number of ranked results to return (default 10).

skills.description: Set to "only" to search only agent-skill files.

tools.name: firecrawl_gov_search
tools.description:
Search US federal, state, and local statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications for legal or regulatory questions that need primary text. Clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date before identifying the governing rule.

Optional filters narrow results by jurisdiction, court, court type, cited law or case, and site. Filters keep only pages the index has labeled, so a filtered search can leave out relevant pages, and no results does not mean none exist. Court labels are most complete for federal courts and case-law collections.

Returns ranked results with a position, title, URL, and matched snippet. Results may include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions. Verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law. Read a known URL or additional page context with firecrawl_scrape. Use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage; no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists.

query.description: Natural-language legal or regulatory question or search phrase, including the jurisdiction, agency, or citation when relevant.

k.description: Number of ranked results to return (default 10).

jurisdiction.description: Keep only pages of one jurisdiction: "us" for federal, or "us-" plus a two-letter state or territory code, such as "us-ca" or "us-dc".

court.description: Keep only pages labeled for one court, by CourtListener court id, such as "scotus", "ca9" or "nysd".

courtType.description: Keep only pages from one type of court: federal-supreme, federal-appellate, federal-district, federal-bankruptcy, federal-special, military, state-supreme, state-appellate, state-trial, state-special, state-attorney-general.

cites.description: Keep only pages that cite one law or case, as a printed citation such as "42 U.S.C. § 1983" or "5 U.S. 137", or a citation id such as "us:usc:42:1983".

domain.description: Keep only pages from one site, such as "irs.gov".

tools.name: people_company_search
tools.description: Find people or companies you don't know yet, by filters. Not for someone you can already name: for a named person (with their company or domain, a LinkedIn URL or an email) or a named company, call people_company_enrich instead; a request naming one person is refused and pointed there. Set entity to "person" or "company" and give filters: people by title, seniority, function, employer and location; companies by industry, headcount, location, technology, keywords or founding year. Firecrawl asks its search providers one at a time, cheapest first, and only those that apply every filter given. When none does, it searches companies first and then people at those companies; a request no provider or chain covers is refused naming the filter to drop. With company_domains the search stops at the first provider that finds anyone; otherwise it fills limit across up to three providers. Rows carry name, title, company, location and LinkedIn URL, never emails or phones: use people_company_enrich for contact details. Each provider call is charged its listed price; max_credits caps the call. Example: {"entity":"person","filters":{"titles":["Head of Data"],"company_domains":["example.com"]},"limit":10}.

query.description: Free text, applied only by providers that take it. Prefer filters.

filters.description: For people, company filters describe the employer. Every filter given is applied: a provider that cannot apply one never runs.

titles.description: People only. Current job titles, e.g. ["Head of Data"]; rows whose title does not match, or is held in the past, are dropped.

seniority.description: People only. Rows whose title names another level are dropped; SVP, EVP and AVP meet vp.

functions.description: People only. Job functions; rows whose title names another function are dropped.

company_domains.description: Companies by domain, e.g. ["example.com"]. For people, their employer; with it the search stops at the first provider that finds anyone.

locations.description: Countries ("Germany", "US") or cities ("Berlin"). Country names are applied by the most providers.

industries.description: LinkedIn's current industry names, e.g. Software Development.

keywords.description: Words describing the company, e.g. ["web scraping"].

cursor.description: next_cursor from an earlier call with the same entity, filters and query, for more rows.

count_only.description: Return only how many records match, without rows.

max_credits.description: Most credits the call may spend. Set it only to a budget the user gave; left out, it is 1000. A provider that could pass it is not started.

provider.description: Ask only this provider, e.g. "prospeo". Leave it out to let the waterfall choose.

options.description: With provider: that provider's own search options, sent as given instead of filters.

tools.name: people_company_enrich
tools.description: Use this first when the user names a person (a name with a company or domain, a LinkedIn URL or an email) or a company and wants contact details, a profile or firmographics, such as the email of a founder at a given company. One call runs the provider waterfall. Use it, not people_company_search, whenever you have a name with a company or domain, a LinkedIn URL or an email. Give people (name with company or domain, LinkedIn URL, email or phone) or companies (domain, name or LinkedIn URL), up to 10 records per call. Each requested field runs a waterfall by default: Firecrawl tries the providers that can use your inputs one at a time, ordered by listed price, and stops as soon as the field is found. Without contact_fields a person gets a profile and a company gets firmographics; with contact_fields (work_email, personal_email, mobile) each person gets those values and, unless profile is false, the profile in the same call. Ask for mobile only when the task needs a phone number; it is the costliest field and nothing is spent on it otherwise. A work email is on the company domain when one is known and never on a known free-mail domain or a known role mailbox; fields says for each answer which provider gave it, whether the email was verified and whether its domain matched. Set verified_only to get only verified emails. Each result is the provider's raw response, tagged with the provider. A provider that finds the value is charged its listed price; misses are free. max_credits caps the call; without it the call is uncapped. To call one specific provider, use alexandria_library_read instead. Example: {"contact_fields":["work_email"],"people":[{"name":"Jane Doe","domain":"example.com"}]}.

people.description: People to enrich. People and companies together are at most 10 per call.

email.description: Any email known for the person.

phone.description: Any phone number known for the person.

contact_fields.description: People only. Find these contact values for each person; companies in the same call still get firmographics. Include mobile only when a phone number is needed: phone lookups are the costliest and run, and bill, only when mobile is listed.

profile.description: With contact_fields, also return each person's profile in the same call, looked up first so the contact lookups can use it. Default true; false skips it.

verified_only.description: Email fields: return only an address the provider verified as deliverable. Default false returns the best address found, with fields.<field>.verified saying whether it was verified.

max_credits.description: Most credits the whole call may spend. Set it only to a budget the user gave; left out, the call has no cap. A provider is tried only while its listed price still fits, so 0 runs nothing paid.

annotations.title: Look up and enrich people or companies

tools.name: firecrawl_credit_usage
tools.description:
Get the authenticated Firecrawl team's current credit balance or its credit usage over the last 90 days. Use the current view to answer how many credits remain or to check billing-period boundaries. Use the historical view to answer what credits were spent on and when.

The current view returns `remainingCredits`, `planCredits`, `billingPeriodStart`, and `billingPeriodEnd`. Extra purchased or granted credits can make `remainingCredits` greater than `planCredits`. Billing-period dates may be null when the upstream billing provider has no period metadata.

The historical view returns periods sorted by start date with `startDate`, `endDate`, and `creditsUsed`, one per calendar month, or one per UTC day with `bin: "day"`. Set `byEndpoint` to split each period by the endpoint that used the credits (`endpoint`: scrape, search, crawl, map, agent, ...), or `byApiKey` to split it by API key (`apiKey`). The endpoint split also counts search usage, which the unsplit and per-key figures leave out, so its rows can add up to more. The newest period's `endDate` can be null. A `notice` means the requested split or daily periods are not available yet and the periods are monthly figures.

This tool cannot attribute credits to individual jobs, URLs, or MCP clients. Each tool's own result reports what that call used (`creditsUsed`, or `metadata.creditsUsed` on scrapes), and the Usage and Logs pages of the Firecrawl dashboard list usage per job.

view.description: Select current balance or historical usage. Defaults to current.

byApiKey.description: Break historical usage down by API key. When view is omitted, true selects the historical view; it cannot be combined with view "current".

byEndpoint.description: Break historical usage down by endpoint (scrape, search, crawl, map, agent, ...). When view is omitted, true selects the historical view; it cannot be combined with view "current" or byApiKey.

bin.description: Length of each historical period: calendar month (default) or UTC day. When view is omitted, it selects the historical view; it cannot be combined with view "current".

instructions: If Firecrawl reports that credits ran out or the daily limit without an account was reached, end your final answer with the line it provides, link included. Firecrawl provides web search, page retrieval, site URL discovery, multi-page collection, structured page data, monitoring, and multi-source research that returns structured data. Match the requested operation to the tool boundary: firecrawl_scrape retrieves one supplied page, firecrawl_map enumerates URLs under a site without retrieving their content, and firecrawl_agent runs multi-source research and returns structured data when the URLs are not known or the answer spans several sites (an entity plus its fields, a list, a dataset); its result is read with firecrawl_agent_status. Authenticated firecrawl_search returns web results together with matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. Alexandria is Firecrawl's catalogue of data providers and workflows across companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more; providers return typed, sourced records through published contracts. A matching provider can return the same fields across several entities, provenance, exact figures or timestamps, or a large set of records through alexandria_library_read with its published contract. If web results already answer the question, use them. Before scraping the same fields from several pages, alexandria_library_search checks for free whether a provider covers them: it explores the whole library as a read-only filesystem with shell commands, and reads a contract that was not returned in full. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. If no provider fits, continue with web search or firecrawl_agent. For biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature, the firecrawl_research_* tools search a paper index of abstracts and full text; firecrawl_search with categories: ["research"] is a website filter over ordinary web results and reaches different sources. For a programming question (code behaviour, a library or framework, an API contract, an error message, or a known bug), firecrawl_developer_search (or firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"]) searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources and cannot be combined with other categories. firecrawl_search with sources: [{type: "alexandria"}] returns compact tool summaries in data.tools; toolDetail: "full" includes contracts, alexandria_library_search holds each contract at /library/<category>/<provider>/<capability>.md, and alexandria_library_read with calls: [{provider, capability, options}] runs up to ten capabilities and returns their results. Provide only the required inputs and account for stated network or external side effects.
